English | 简体中文 · v0.3.1 research preview · MIT · Python 3.10+"},{"id":"p3s1","text":"I got tired of re-explaining my project to every new AI chat, and then getting the old version of a "},{"id":"p3s2","text":" re-explaining my project to every new AI chat, and then getting the old version of a decision back."},{"id":"p4s1","text":"**When a fact changes, only the latest version comes back.**"},{"id":"p5s1","text":"Say your project chat moved from Flask to Django, then FastAPI, then Litestar. TOMC Memory hands you"},{"id":"p5s2","text":"r assistant `framework = Litestar`, plus the line it came from."},{"id":"p6s1","text":"**After installing, say to your assistant: "Try TOMC Memory".** In a terminal: `tomc try`."},{"id":"p7s1","text":"- **Latest value, offline check (v0.3.0):** 144 questions per budget, each about a fact that changed"},{"id":"p7s2","text":" 3 to 5 times. At the default budget the prepared context held the latest value every time (v0.2.1: "},{"id":"p7s3","text":"58%). At a 10% budget: 85% (v0.2.1: 51%). Synthetic notes and chats, no model call. We wrote these q"},{"id":"p7s4","text":"uestions alongside the fixes, so treat them as our regression test, not an independent evaluation.
-"},{"id":"p7s5","text":" **Smaller requests in Codex (0.1.0 preview, not re-run since):** 9 synthetic project chats of about"},{"id":"p7s6","text":" 10K to 40K tokens, 5 questions each, `gpt-6.1-sol`. Keeping 40% of the history cut request input by"},{"id":"p7s7","text":" 29.7% on average, and all 45 answers stayed right. One run per condition.
- **BEAM long-history ben"},{"id":"p7s8","text":"chmark (paper experiments):** same reader model on both sides, 3 readers, 6 other memory methods. TO"},{"id":"p7s9","text":"MC had the higher mean score in 54 of 54 comparisons at 500K to 10M tokens, and 17 of 18 at 100K. Me"},{"id":"p7s10","text":"an scores only; not comparable with other projects' BEAM numbers."},{"id":"p8s1","text":"Every number, with its conditions and failures · Before you use it · Install"},{"id":"p9s1","text":"## Before you use it"},{"id":"p10s1","text":"1. **It does not shrink the chat your assistant is already having.** Claude Code and Codex manage th"},{"id":"p10s2","text":"eir own chat. TOMC Memory works on history you hand it and notes you saved. Context ownership
2. **S"},{"id":"p10s3","text":"hort histories gain little.** Under about 10K tokens there is not much to cut. With the default budg"},{"id":"p10s4","text":"et, our earlier tests saved roughly 10–20% of input (Codex 9.2%, Claude API-style 19.8%; 0.1.0 previ"},{"id":"p10s5","text":"ews). Smaller budgets save more but can drop the latest value. Check them on your own tasks first. T"},{"id":"p10s6","text":"he default keeps 80% of a history up to 10K tokens, sliding to 60% at 1M, and never less than 1,024 "},{"id":"p10s7","text":"tokens.
3. **It matches words, not meaning.** A reworded update such as "scratch that, go with Djang"},{"id":"p10s8","text":"o" can be missed, mostly at small budgets. When a later line may have changed a value, the value is "},{"id":"p10s9","text":"marked `STATE?` and that line is attached so you or your assistant can check it.
4. **What gets stor"},{"id":"p10s10","text":"ed, and how to erase it.** Results of `prepare_context` and `recall_memory` are not saved unless you"},{"id":"p10s11","text":" turn it on (`tomc settings --save-mcp-results on`). Notes you save with `remember_memory` stay on y"},{"id":"p10s12","text":"our computer in `~/.tomc/memory.sqlite3`. Delete one notebook with `forget_memory`, or everything wi"},{"id":"p10s13","text":"th `tomc erase-all --yes`. Security and privacy
5. **Not every client is checked.** Codex and Claude"},{"id":"p10s14","text":" Code passed real model calls with earlier previews. For Cursor, TRAE and WorkBuddy the setup is wri"},{"id":"p10s15","text":"tten, but their tool calls have not been checked on real machines. Claude Desktop installation has n"},{"id":"p10s16","text":"ot been checked in the app.
6. **The paper is not public yet.** The benchmark numbers come from our "},{"id":"p10s17","text":"own runs and setup. The evidence page lists sources, sample sizes and what can be rechecked offline "},{"id":"p10s18","text":" The evidence page lists sources, sample sizes and what can be rechecked offline (`make reproduce`)."},{"id":"p11s1","text":"## Install"},{"id":"p12s1","text":"Each path ends the same way: say **"Try TOMC Memory"** in a new chat, and run `tomc doctor` if somet"},{"id":"p12s2","text":"hing looks wrong. The Claude Code and Codex plugins need uv. Running from source needs Python 3.10 o"},{"id":"p12s3","text":"r newer (`python3 --version`; the macOS system Python 3.9 is too old)."},{"id":"p13s1","text":"### Claude Code"},{"id":"p14s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p15s1","text":"Start a new session, check `/mcp` for `plugin:tomc-memory:tomc`, then say "Try TOMC Memory" or run `"},{"id":"p15s2","text":"/tomc-memory:try`.
